feature: A logo or picture clip on a Gfx track is amber
summary: A picture or logo you lay over a video now sits on its Gfx track as an amber clip, the colour the title mock draws, so it stands apart from the recording on V1 and from titles.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a screen recording and pause two seconds in.
File > Import Media (Shift Command I) and bring in a PNG logo.
Drag the logo's tile from the Library onto V1 at two seconds and let go.
Click an empty spot on the canvas so nothing is picked, and look at the Gfx track.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Switch the Mac to Light appearance and read the clip's name again.
try.shotNote: Drawn by the legibility check, not the live window: the clip on the light panel.

evaluate: Does the logo's amber clip read as a different kind of thing from the recording on V1 at a glance?
Is the dark brown name on the amber easy to read in both light and dark?
Does the amber feel at home beside the teal-to-violet V1 clip and the dark Title clip, or is it too loud?
rough: The mock prints the clip's name in white; white on this amber reads 1.8:1 and fails the legibility check, so the name is a deep brown instead (the user's legibility rule, your call on 2026-09-30, and this task's own checklist).
Folded tracks (the collapsed strip) also take the amber for a Gfx clip, which the mock does not draw; matches the colour the open track uses.
